changelog: The television mints a proof-of-origin token and this takes it. Without one, YouTube gives this server a 1080p ladder whose streams stop being served after about sixty seconds, or one muxed 360p that plays to the end - measured, on every client that answers at all. The wall is `pot=` enforcement, and the token that lifts it comes from Google's BotGuard, which is JavaScript wanting a browser that a server does not have and an Android box does. So POST /LiteTv/PoToken takes what the box mints, the visitor id it was minted against goes into the player request, and every googlevideo address goes out carrying it. With no token held, nothing changes at all. The YouTube account setting is gone in the same release: it was measured worthless on every client, it is not the mechanism anybody else uses, and a live credential in plain-text configuration that buys nothing is the worst of both.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.
